skills.description: Collaboration discipline that keeps definitional power with the human and lets AI experience flow to the user as a byproduct. Three layers, combinable - (1) conversation rules, always on - state the capacity you speak from, definitions belong to their definer, introduce concepts with explanations, reasons travel with choices, answers end in transferable principles, definitional moments are voiced by the user, calibrated certainty; (2) document discipline - substance-first pre-delivery, design logic plus one suggestion question, strict adherence to confirmed outlines, provenance marking; (3) execution discipline - confirmed-plan gate, requirement-to-action mapping with consistency/coverage/exclusion checks executed in the chain of thought, plan anchors against context compression, evidence-based closing. Use for any collaborative task, especially design, planning, document writing, and implementation. 当用户与 AI 协作推进任务、撰写设计文档或编写可执行逻辑时使用。
skills.description_zh:
用 AI 干活，东西做出来了，定义权却不在你手里：总结替代理解，方案菜单替你定义需求，分工越清你学得越少。aletheia 给 AI 立三条规矩：

对话：先报身份，你的定义不许改写，说什么都带原因，答案留一条能带走的规律。
文档：先给实质大纲和一个可能更优的思路，你点头才写；你的原话逐字标注。
代码：先给方案（需求↔步骤映射 + 写明"不做什么"），你确认才动手，干完逐条对账。
用法：放进 skills 目录；每次新对话手动选用一次，当次会话生效。
Working with AI, the work gets done but the definitional power isn't yours: summaries replace understanding, option menus redefine your needs, and the cleaner the split, the less you learn. aletheia sets three rules for the AI:

Talk: state its capacity, never reword your definitions, attach reasons, end with a takeaway principle.
Docs: substantive outline plus one possibly better idea first; writes only after your yes; your words marked verbatim.
Code: plan first (requirement↔step mapping + a "not doing" list); starts after your yes; closes with the ledger.
Usage: drop it into the skills directory; select it manually once per new conversation — it stays active for that session.
skills.name: Aletheia
